# Updating the toolkit from GitHub

People find the toolkit on Nexus and download it there once. **Every later update comes from the toolkit's GitHub
releases, done by you.** The session start says, once per version, when a newer release is out. Nothing is installed
until the user says yes; after applying, setup runs and the guards are checked, and a failure rolls the update back.

Run every command from the toolkit folder (the game folder the toolkit was extracted into). `python` is the Python
the hooks use (`SKYGUARD_PYTHON` in `skyrim-paths.env`).

**If the session start said `TOOLKIT UPDATE NEEDS THE USER`**, stop here: an earlier update failed or was
interrupted and the guards are unverified. Tell the user at once and go to section 6.

## 1. Check

```bash
python tools/agent-harness.py update-check --now
```

`update_available: true` names `installed` and `latest`. Tell the user, in one line, which version is out and ask
whether to update now. `status: unreachable` means GitHub could not be reached: say so, do not retry in a loop.
`status: off` means the user turned checking off (`.modding-agent-harness/updates.json`); honour it unless they ask.
If `error` is set with `status: off`, that file exists but cannot be read (checking stays off until it is fixed):
tell the user, and that `{"v": 1, "check": false}` (or deleting the file) is the valid form.

## 2. Stage the review (changes nothing installed)

```bash
python tools/agent-harness.py update-stage --installed-root .
```

It downloads the release into a per-user folder outside the toolkit folder and **refuses** it unless the SHA-256
matches the digest GitHub publishes, every zip entry is safe under one folder, and the zip's `BUILD-INFO` names the
release's version and the commit its tag points at. Then it compares the release with this install. A refusal
(`ok: false`, exit 2) is final: report the `error` and stop; never work around it (no manual download, no copying
over the install, no plain `upgrade-*` commands, which skip the health check and the rollback).

The JSON gives `review` (the text to show), `bundle`, `review_sha256` and `requires_guard_accept`. The review ends
with a `next:` block naming the choices file and the exact `update-apply` arguments.

## 3. Show the user, then ask

Show, in this order:
1. What the new version brings: its section of the new `CHANGELOG.md` (the top heading, in the release unpacked
   beside the bundle), in a few lines.
2. **Every guard change in full** (the review's diffs): code that decides what the agent may do. When
   `requires_guard_accept` is true, applying needs the user's **separate, explicit go for those guard changes**, on
   top of their go for the update. Ask for it on its own; never assume one yes covers both.
3. **Every collision, one line each, with your recommendation** (`preserve_collision`: a file whose bytes match
   neither what the installed release shipped nor the new one). Marked "unchanged upstream, keep is lossless": the
   new release did not change it, recommend `keep`. For the rest, a file the user (or another session) edited is
   theirs: recommend `keep` and say what they would miss from the new version. A file setup generates (the agent
   instruction files, the hook definitions, hook scripts with filled-in paths) is regenerated by setup after the
   update: recommend `candidate`. A project settings file: recommend `merged_settings` (their own settings kept, the
   new hooks taken), except `keep` for a settings file that still holds setup's unfilled double-brace placeholders,
   which belongs to an agent this install never set up. A file under "Only if you choose `candidate`" is guard code
   they changed themselves: `keep` is lossless; `candidate` needs the same separate guard go.
4. That nothing is replaced until they say yes, that setup and a guard check run afterwards, and that a failure is
   rolled back automatically.

Never decide a collision silently, and never pick `candidate` for a file the user edited without their explicit yes
for that file. Their notes (`KNOWLEDGEBASE.local.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`), `skyrim-paths.env` and local settings are
always kept.

## 4. Apply (only after the user's yes)

Write their choices, one JSON object `{"path": "keep" | "candidate" | "merged_settings", ...}` with one entry per
collision and per merged settings file, to the choices file the review names. Ask them to close any other agent
session or editor working in this folder. Then run the review's `update-apply` line, prefixed with
`python tools/agent-harness.py` and with `--installed-root .`, **in the background** (setup and the check may each
take up to 10 minutes):

```bash
python tools/agent-harness.py update-apply --installed-root . --bundle "<bundle>" --review-sha256 "<review_sha256>" \
    --choices "<choices file>" --quiescent
```

Add `--accept-guard-changes` only when the user gave the separate go for the guard changes in step 3.

After replacing the files, it runs `bash setup.sh --agent auto` and `tools/skyguard/update_canary.py`. The canary
requires each configured agent's installed hooks to refuse a raw plugin write. It also checks that any harmless
command it probes is allowed. When the release changes setup or the canary, the pre-update check runs too.

## 5. Report

- **`ok: true` (exit 0):** tell the user the version now installed and the operation ID; that
  `python tools/agent-harness.py upgrade-rollback <operation ID> --installed-root . --quiescent` undoes it; to
  **restart the agent session** (hooks and instructions load at session start), and on Codex to approve the changed
  hooks in its hook review; and, if `Data/SKSE/Plugins/ToolkitProbe.dll` exists, that the release also carries a
  `ToolkitProbe.zip` to install through their mod manager (never copy it into `Data` yourself). Then run
  `bash tools/hook-canary.sh` after a few real tool calls in the new session.
- **`ok: false`, `rolled_back: true` (exit 1):** the update was undone. Show the `report` (the failed step's output)
  and stop; the installed version is unchanged.
- **`ok: false` otherwise, or any exit 1 without a report:** the update failed and could not be rolled back and
  verified. Tell the user at once and go to section 6.
- **Exit 2:** refused before anything changed; report the `error`.

## 6. A failed or interrupted update

`.modding-agent-harness/update-failed.json` (a rollback or the old check failed) or
`.modding-agent-harness/update-in-flight.json` (an apply is running or was interrupted) means the guards may be
broken. Staging and applying refuse while either exists. Show the user the file, help them fix the cause (roll back
the operation it names with `upgrade-rollback`, or re-run `bash setup.sh --agent auto` and
`python tools/skyguard/update_canary.py --root .`), and only once they confirm it is fixed:

```bash
python tools/agent-harness.py update-clear-failed --installed-root .
```

It sets both aside (renamed, kept) and refuses while the recorded apply is still running; `--force` overrides that
once the user is sure it has ended.

Each `update-stage` downloads into a fresh folder, so trying again later just works. Older downloads in the updates
folder are not removed by the update; once an update is applied and the user is happy with it, offer to move the
older ones to the Recycle Bin (the rollback record lives in the install, not in them).
